title: Canonical dualizing base-change mate under composition
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes, without absolute separatedness; all arrows are $k$-morphisms. Use $D^b_{ctf}$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], on small pro-etale sites, and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a separated finite-type arrow $u:T\to U$, write $F_u=Ru_!$, $G_u=Ru^!$ for compact supports and its transported constructible exceptional right adjoint [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $\varepsilon_u:F_uG_u\to1$ for its counit, and $\omega_u=G_u\Lambda_U$. Use the specified canonical tensor map $\theta_{u,P}:Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u\to G_uP$ and dualizing base-change map $\beta_{u,v}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; these maps are defined without assuming cohomological smoothness. All unit, symmetry and reassociation maps are the canonical derived ones.

Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms. Let $t:Z'\to Z$ be arbitrary between finite-type $k$-schemes, put $Y'=Y\times_ZZ'$ and $X'=X\times_ZZ'$, and write $h:Y'\to Y$, $s:X'\to X$, $g':Y'\to Z'$, $f':X'\to Y'$ for the projections. For $u=f,g,gf$ use its compactification and the base-changed compactification, and the specified compact-support exchanges. Let $c:G_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fG_g$ and $c':G_{g'f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f'}G_{g'}$ be the counit-preserving conjugates of canonical compact-support composition [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], as in [lem-pur-constructible-tensor-composition]; only its unconditional compositor construction is used. Define $b_{f,h;P}:Ls^*G_fP\to G_{f'}Lh^*P$, for $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, as the transpose of $Lh^*\varepsilon_{f,P}\circ E_f(G_fP)^{-1}$ under $F_{f'}\dashv G_{f'}$, that is, the base-change morphism of [pur9-cs-def-bc] computed with the base-changed compactification for $f'$. Then the actual dualizing base-change morphism of the composite satisfies
$$\beta_{gf,t}=c_{\Lambda_{Z'}}'^{-1}\circ G_{f'}(\beta_{g,t})\circ b_{f,h;\omega_g}\circ Ls^*(c_{\Lambda_Z}).$$
Both sides are morphisms $Ls^*\omega_{gf}\to\omega_{g'f'}$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X',\Lambda)$, with the coefficient-unit pullback identifications inserted. This is an equality of the specified counit mates, including the vertical-pasting normalization of compact-support exchange; it holds without cohomological smoothness or invertibility assumptions on the dualizing base-change maps.

proof.text: Put $A=Ls^*$, $B=Lh^*$, $C=Lt^*$ and $H=gf$. Write $\alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_H$ and $\alpha':F_{g'}F_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g'f'}$ for compact-support composition. All expressions below are on the bounded-below etale-origin class: every $G_uK$ in use is bounded constructible by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], hence has an origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Pullbacks retain the witnesses as in [pur9-cs-def-bc], and compact supports retain the class by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Use the natural Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], not ambient pro-etale adjunctions. Their compactification dimension bounds exist by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Thus single and iterated transposes of the displayed maps are defined and injective. The conjugates $c,c'$ use the composite Hom bijections of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]; in particular their counits are the pasted counits.

proof.text:
Choose a compatible compactification tower for $f,g$ by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], and its pullback along $t$. Let $E_f:BF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}A$, $E_g:CF_g\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g'}B$, and $E_H:CF_H\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g'f'}A$ be the specified exchanges. The compact-support vertical interchange is
$$E_H\circ C(\alpha)=(\alpha'A)\circ(F_{g'}E_f)\circ(E_gF_f).\tag{1}$$
Here is the precise existing input for this equality. Apply [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-composition-pasting-coherence] with its $h=g$ and base map $g=t$ to constant strict towers over $B_{\rm coeff}=\Lambda$, and evaluate at one index. Its displayed vertical interchange is (1). Each evaluation of the constant input has the bounded-below finite-coefficient origin witness from Step 1. [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] identifies the evaluated proper/open and refinement maps with the normalized finite proper/open maps; [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations] specifies evaluation comparisons by the termwise inverse image and its direct-image mate. Thus $D,D'$ evaluate to the canonical tower compositors $\alpha,\alpha'$, and $e_f,e_g,e_H$ to the proper-mate/open exchanges. By [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] these are precisely the transported exchanges used here, independent of the chosen witnesses. The refinement equation in the same coherence node moves (1) from this compatible tower to the prescribed compactifications and their base changes. This only applies a functor to an equality already in the tower category; it does not infer an equality from evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, lemma-base-change-shriek: vertical stacking compatibility with Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition; finite pro-etale transport and counit-mate calculation supplied below

proof.text:
All three exchanges in (1) are invertible on this class by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Multiplying (1) on the left by $E_H^{-1}$ and on the right by $(\alpha'A)^{-1}$, then cancelling, gives the equality of inverse-exchange squares
$$C(\alpha)\circ(E_g^{-1}F_f)\circ(F_{g'}E_f^{-1})=E_H^{-1}\circ(\alpha'A).\tag{2}$$
Both sides have source $F_{g'}F_{f'}A$ and target $CF_H$. Only compact-support exchanges, not exceptional base-change maps, were inverted.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, lemma-base-change-shriek: vertical stacking compatibility with Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition; finite pro-etale transport and counit-mate calculation supplied below

proof.text:
Take mates of (2). Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] says that the mate of $(E_g^{-1}F_f)\circ(F_{g'}E_f^{-1})$ under the two composite adjunctions is
$G_{f'}(b_{g,t})\circ(b_{f,h}G_g)$.
Clauses (3)(b) and (3)(a), applied respectively to $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$, identify the mates of the left and right sides of (2) as
$$G_{f'}(b_{g,t})\circ(b_{f,h}G_g)\circ A(c),\qquad c'C\circ b_{H,t}.$$
Indeed $\alpha:F_gF_f\to F_H$ has conjugate $c:G_H\to G_fG_g$ and likewise for primes, with the prescribed counits [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]; [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] fixes this direction. The individual mates are exactly the maps $b$ of [pur9-cs-def-bc], since their adjuncts are pulled-back counit after inverse exchange. Consequently for every constructible finite-Tor $K$,
$$c'_{CK}\circ b_{H,t;K}=G_{f'}(b_{g,t;K})\circ b_{f,h;G_gK}\circ A(c_K).\tag{3}$$
This use of mate calculus is on the relative Hom bijections from Step 1; equivalently compute the same double transpose there. It requires only their naturality and injectivity, which that cited theorem supplies, not a right adjoint on the entire pro-etale derived category.

source.place: Tag 0E46, remark-compose-base-change; explicit adjunction pasting via lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting clauses (2), (3)(a),(3)(b), as in Mathlib CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean

proof.text:
Set $K=\Lambda_Z$ in (3). Write $u:C\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{Z'}$ for the coefficient-unit identification. By [def-pur-co-smoothness] and [pur9-cs-def-bc],
$\beta_{g,t}=G_{g'}(u)\circ b_{g,t;\Lambda_Z}$ and $\beta_{H,t}=G_{g'f'}(u)\circ b_{H,t;\Lambda_Z}$.
Naturality of $c'$ at $u$ gives
$$c'_{\Lambda_{Z'}}\circ G_{g'f'}(u)=G_{f'}G_{g'}(u)\circ c'_{C\Lambda_Z}.$$
Postcompose (3) by $G_{f'}G_{g'}(u)$, substitute these two beta formulas and $G_g\Lambda_Z=\omega_g$, and cancel the isomorphism $c'_{\Lambda_{Z'}}$. This is exactly
$$\beta_{gf,t}=c_{\Lambda_{Z'}}'^{-1}\circ G_{f'}(\beta_{g,t})\circ b_{f,h;\omega_g}\circ Ls^*(c_{\Lambda_Z}).$$
The source is $Ls^*\omega_{gf}$ and the target is $\omega_{g'f'}$. This final substitution uses neither smoothness nor invertibility of any $b$ or $\beta$.
